id_and_class.theory_title: Owen’s Mind-Body Powers: NCC are Philosophically and Religiously Neutral
id_and_class.summary: Matthew Owen argues that the search for neural correlates of consciousness (NCC) commits no one to physicalism, so atheist materialists and theistic dualists can pursue it together. His own Mind-Body Powers model reads NCC through Aristotelian-Thomistic hylomorphism: neural mechanisms and conscious states are the joint manifestation of a person's bodily and mental powers, and consciousness is prior to its neural mechanisms.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as a Mental Power Co-Manifesting with the Brain

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a power of the soul, the form that unifies a living human body. Conscious states are manifestations of that mental power, paired with bodily powers expressed in neural mechanisms.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and body are form and matter of one subject. Following Aquinas, the body and its parts exist so that the soul can manifest its powers, which requires a ‘well-ordered brain’; neural mechanisms exist because the body is unified by a form with the power to be conscious.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not emergent; Owen rejects the view that consciousness emerges from the brain and holds it to be ontologically prior to its neural mechanisms.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Every conscious state has a bearer, the conscious subject or creature. Owen treats accounting for this subject as possibly the hardest problem, harder than phenomenal feel or unity.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Substantial forms (souls) that are metaphysically simple; mental and bodily powers; neurons and neurotransmitters as the matter through which powers manifest.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through NCC research, which seeks the minimal neuronal mechanisms sufficient for consciousness, interpreted within an Aristotelian metaphysics of causation.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A unified subject whose form carries mental powers and whose body carries biological powers, the two manifesting together at cellular and sub-cellular levels.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal; unity of experience; the conscious subject; mental causation
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Co-manifestation of mind-body powers. NCC exist because neural correlates and conscious states jointly express interdependent bodily and mental powers.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Either side can lead. Bodily powers often instigate a conscious state, as when one sees a face; a mental power can instigate neural activity, as when one consciously signs a check.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Neural mechanisms in human brains and many animal brains, as parts of a body unified by a single form.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Conscious states cause physical events in the body. Owen notes that it can be legally vital that a conscious intention to sign a check caused the neural events of signing.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Unity is given by the single form, so there is no need to explain how a unified experience arises from countless neural parts.
core_claims_and_evidence: Crick and Koch meant ‘correlates’ to be ontologically neutral, and Koch cites Owen's model as a nonphysicalist reading of NCC.
Reductive physicalism has not managed to reduce consciousness to its neural substrate.
Non-reductive physicalism faces Kim's exclusion problem: supervening conscious states risk losing any causal role to their neural base.
The hylomorphic framework has been applied to measuring consciousness, detecting it in brain-injured patients, and assessing brain organoids.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical (Aristotelian and Thomistic metaphysics) applied to empirical NCC research.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Applications to measuring consciousness, detecting it in unresponsive brain-injured patients, and evaluating brain organoid consciousness; current work extends the model to artificial neural networks.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Physicalists can argue, following Smart, that reductive physicalism gives the most parsimonious explanation of NCC. The neutrality claim sits alongside a model that is itself explicitly dualist and theologically motivated.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent within Aristotelian-Thomistic hylomorphism, and Owen presents it as one admissible foundation among others for an NCC science that requires none of the ‘-isms’.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Owen is applying the model to artificial neural networks, but on hylomorphism consciousness is a power of the form of a living body, and he gives no verdict on machines.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Owen holds that the hylomorphic framework is compatible with life after death and gives warrant for anticipating bodily resurrection.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: The model is designed to welcome atheists and theists alike, though its Thomistic roots fit a theistic picture.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Since consciousness belongs to the unifying form of a living body and is prior to neural mechanisms, copying those mechanisms would not carry the subject over.
